newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen slightly lower at open after record.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen slightly lower at open after record.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open slightly lower on Monday, hurt by weakness in oil stocks and profit-taking after Friday's record close.
But market sentiment is expected to remain strong, with many investors now discounting the possibility of a sharp hike in interest rates by the Fed this month.
On Friday, the Dow industrials jumped 67 to an unofficial record 5839, its first close above 5800. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composte also posted strong gains.
"We might be headed for a slightly lower opening and then some stabilization ... and an attempt to move higher," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"I suspect we'll see profit-taking. Also, Iraq is putting pressure on the oil market which could weaken oil stocks," he said.
November Brent crude futures have fallen well off the post-Gulf War peak of $24.39 touched on Thursday by the expired oil contract.
The long-bond was off 3/32 to yield 6.96 percent.

"We won't have a repeat of Friday, although I suspect we will hit 5875 sometime early this week," he said. Friday's 'triple witching' expiration of options and some minor economic data could affect the market this week.

Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock and Co, said: "All eyes are on corporate earnings as the market tries to hold its high ground and add to its gains. We could see some early profit-taking."
"A rate hike of 50 basis points seems to be not a concern for the market. That's the powerhouse, the catalyst for this market to move higher in the coming weeks," Cardillo said.
Standard & Poor's December futures were up 0.45 to 689.30.
At 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, July business inventories are due. They are expected to rise 0.2 percent compared to a 0.1 percent jump in June.
Tokyo stocks were closed for the "Respect for the Aged" national holiday.
In London, U.S. shares were little moved in quiet trading. The FTSE 100 was up 6.5 to 3974.4.
The dollar was strongly supported in late Asia trading and was locked in narrow ranges in quiet Europe trading.
General Motors has been hinting at possible plans to shed its Hughes Electronics unit, according to the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street Column.
